scope: CPU-only comparison of BindingDB 2026-08 rows explicitly tagged Curation/DataSource=ChEMBL against the local ChEMBL 37 SQLite release. No canonical files or models were modified.

comparison_key.combined_identity: A row is matched if either its explicit ChEMBL ligand ID key or its exact InChIKey key occurs in ChEMBL 37 with the same sorted UniProt set, endpoint, relation, and numeric nM value.
comparison_key.endpoint_policy: Kd, Ki, IC50, and EC50 remain distinct.
comparison_key.relation_policy: Exact (=), left-censored (<), and right-censored (>) values remain distinct. No censor relation was converted to an exact value.
comparison_key.numeric_policy: BindingDB endpoint fields are already in nM; single relation-plus-number strings were parsed and compared numerically to ChEMBL standard_value where standard_units=nM.
comparison_key.reason_not_in_key: BindingDB's full TSV does not expose the originating ChEMBL activity ID, so this is a standardized measurement-key existence comparison, not a one-to-one source-record reconciliation.

compound_and_target_coverage.inchikey_mismatch_interpretation: Not automatically an error: salt stripping, parent mapping, protonation, stereochemistry, or release drift can change an InChIKey while an upstream ligand ID remains related. These rows require structure-aware reconciliation.

derivation.lower: max(2,864,273 ChEMBL resolved keys, 1,539,331 BindingDB combined-identity keys)

defensible_union.interpretation: 2,864,273 is conservative if every currently unmatched BindingDB key is an alias/version-drift duplicate. 3,266,356 treats all 402,083 unmatched combined-identity keys as distinct. The true identity-reconciled union should lie inside this range under the stated key domain.
defensible_union.do_not_confuse_with: physical source rows, assays, citations, or unique ligand-target pairs; repeated assays with the same standardized key collapse here.

limitations: An unmatched key is not proof of a new experiment; it can reflect compound parent/salt/stereo differences, target isoform/version changes, altered censor/value formatting, or a ChEMBL release difference.
An existence match is not a one-to-one activity-row match because BindingDB omits the originating ChEMBL activity ID.

The comparison uses all ChEMBL 37 nM rows for the four endpoints, not only the platform's narrower 2,117,384-row binding task subset, because BindingDB's ChEMBL import spans assay and target categories.
No assay-level or citation-level evidence was deleted or averaged.

validation.bindingdb_measurement_arithmetic: 1,229,978 matched + 428,175 unmatched = 1,658,153 eligible; two of 1,658,155 endpoint rows lack a combined identity route
